t.2.87.2: Bears, herds of spotted deer, and ruru deer are seen all around, in the rows of forest, on the mountains, and along the rivers.
t.2.87.4: The army of the great-souled Bharata, resembling the surging flood of the ocean, covered the earth as a rain-cloud covers the sky in the monsoon season.
t.2.87.5: Covered over by masses of horses and by elephants of great speed, the earth at that time became invisible for a long while.
t.2.87.6: Having traveled a long way, his mounts utterly exhausted, the glorious Bharata spoke to Vasiṣṭha, the foremost of counselors.
t.2.87.7: Judging by the appearance that is seen here, and just as I have heard it described, we have clearly reached that region of which Bharadvāja spoke.
t.2.87.8: This is Mount Citrakūṭa, and that is the river Mandākinī; this forest, resembling a dark-blue cloud, shines forth from afar.
t.2.87.9: The lovely slopes of Mount Citrakūṭa are even now being trampled by my mountain-like elephants.
t.2.87.10: These trees on the mountain slopes shed their flowers, just as dark, dense rain-bearing clouds release their water when the season of heat has passed.
t.2.87.11: Look, Śatrughna, at this mountain whose regions are frequented by Kiṃnaras, now covered all around with horses, like the ocean filled with makaras.
t.2.87.12: These herds of deer, startled into swift flight, look like a line of clouds in the autumn sky driven along by the wind.
t.2.87.13: These ones wear fragrant chaplets of flowers upon their heads and bear shields gleaming like clouds, just as the men of the south do.
t.2.87.15: The dust raised by the hooves stands covering the sky, and the wind carries it swiftly along, as if doing what is dear to me.
t.2.87.14: This forest, dreadful to behold, having fallen as if silent, now appears to me like Ayodhyā thronged with people.
t.2.87.17: Look at these frightened peacocks, so lovely to behold, as they enter this mountain, the dwelling place of birds.
t.2.87.16: Look, Śatrughna, at these chariots yoked with horses and driven by the foremost charioteers, rushing swiftly through the forest.
t.2.87.18: This region seems exceedingly delightful to me. Clearly this is a dwelling of ascetics, like a path to heaven.
t.2.87.19: In the forest many spotted deer are seen together with their does, lovely in form, as though painted with flowers.
t.2.87.20: Let the soldiers set out in good order and search the forest thoroughly, so that those two tigers among men, Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa, may be seen.
t.2.87.21: Hearing Bharata's words, the brave men, weapons in hand, entered that forest, and then they saw smoke.
t.2.87.22: Having seen the column of smoke, they returned and said to Bharata: "Fire does not occur where there are no men; clearly the two Rāghavas are right here."
t.2.87.23: Or else, if those two princes, tigers among men and scorchers of foes, were not here, then clearly there are other ascetics here who are like Rāma.
t.2.87.1: Harassed by that great advancing army, the rutting leaders of the forest-dweller's herds fled away in all directions together with their herds.
t.2.87.24: Having heard that speech of theirs, approved by the good, Bharata, crusher of enemy forces, spoke to all those soldiers.
t.2.87.25: Let you all remain here, vigilant; no one is to go forward from this place. I alone shall go, and Sumantra and our preceptor as well.
t.2.87.26: Thus addressed, they all then stood there on every side, while Bharata fixed his gaze on the place where the tip of the smoke rose.
t.2.87.27: That army which had been halted by Bharata, gazing at the smoke ahead, then became joyful, knowing that before long it would meet with beloved Rāma.
t.2.87.3: That righteous-souled son of Daśaratha, well pleased, set forth, surrounded by a great and clamorous army of four divisions.
